description: Shared fixtures for the link-preview metadata of the web server (Share/14, #436, docs/operations/link-previews.md): the card of a deck or of an author that nginx puts into the head of index.html for /d/{code}/{slug}, so Telegram, VK and search engines see the deck without server-side rendering. GET and HEAD only, the public chain of the deck reads (same limiter, bulkhead and kill switch), a guest's view that never depends on a token. The /head fragment is served as text/plain with a restrictive Content-Security-Policy because it is reachable on the application origin. Every case that is not a PUBLIC deck (or a profile with a public card) is the SAME generic card, so the answer is not an oracle. All JSON strings are plain text; the HTML fragment is the only markup and has every value escaped. `invariants` are executable: PublicMetaContractFixtureTest builds these examples with the production code.

constants.authorCardTimeout: 150 ms, cached 60 s; any failure leaves the author out
constants.canonicalHeader: X-Mnema-Canonical: /d/{code}/{slug}, on the /head answer of a PUBLIC deck only; the web server compares it with the requested path and answers 301 on a difference
constants.previewHeader: X-Mnema-Preview: card|generic on every /head answer (the web server reports card|generic|redirect|fallback on the page)
constants.robotsHeader: X-Robots-Tag: noindex on the /head answer of the generic card (the web server puts it on the page)

routes.answer: text/plain;charset=UTF-8 head fragment with Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; sandbox, X-Mnema-Preview, and for a PUBLIC deck X-Mnema-Canonical; the generic card also answers X-Robots-Tag: noindex. No query parameter changes the answer.
text/plain;charset=UTF-8 head fragment, same headers (no canonical header)

invariants: the JSON of every non-public case equals `generic.json` byte for byte, and so does the fragment; no canonical header is ever sent for them
the JSON has exactly the members kind, title, description, canonical, robots, image, author in this order
a title or description is one line of plain text, cut on a word boundary with an ellipsis, at most 120 and 200 code points

a title, description or name is one line of plain text: whitespace and control characters become one space, bidirectional formatting characters (U+200E/F, U+202A-202E, U+2066-2069, U+061C) are dropped
the fragment has one tag per line and only title, meta and link tags; & < > " ' in a value are character references, so a value cannot open a tag, a comment (<!--) or an SSI directive
the fragment replaces the whole default block of frontend/src/index.html: it declares every name and property that block declares (and `author` besides)
problem answers (404 disabled, 429, 503) stay no-store; the web server turns every status of 300 and above into the plain index.html
